SAP: DIRTY MONEY

By: Sasha OLD | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We all blame the Guptas for the mess we're left with, but what about the lives they ruined - we speak exclusively to a man who stood between them and 100 million in alleged kickbacks.

Unique Selling Point:
When you look at our State Owned Enterprises today, after several years of ‘Gupta Capture,’ you realize they were Ground Zero for brothers Ajay, Atul and Rajesh who leveraged their close proximity to then-President Jacob Zuma in order to extract unprecedented tenders. IT’S UNKNOWN HOW MANY BILLIONS STATE CAPTURE HAS COST SOUTH AFRICA’S ECONOMY. BUT THIS STORY IS NOT JUST A GUPTA ONE, IT’S ABOUT INTERNATIONAL COMPANIES USING THE GUPTA SERVICE TO PROFIT, AND THEN STAYING “WILFULLY BLIND” AFTER THE FACT. AND IT’S ALSO A NEW STORY SHOWING HOW AN UNSUSPECTING SMALL COMPANY WAS CAUGHT IN THE MIDDLE - USED AND THEN LEFT WITH NOTHING.
Enter German Software Multinational SAP; They trade on the New York Stock Exchange, have offices in America and London and made R450 billion last year. BUT WHEN SAP WAS HAVING PROBLEMS CLOSING BIG DEALS WITH OUR SOE’S ON ITS OWN, DOCUMENTS SHOWED THEY TURNED TO THE BROTHERS FOR THEIR POLITICAL INFLUENCE. A SMALL GUPTA OWNED 3D PRINTING COMPANY WAS USED AS A FRONT TO BOTH DISTANCE ITSELF FROM TRANSACTIONS, HIDING THE GUPTA CONNECTION, BUT ALSO TO LAUNDER THE PROCEEDS OF SUCCESSFULLY ACQUIRED CONTRACTS FOR SAP TO THEMSELVES.THAT front company was CAD house, whose owner Bernhard Voigt is speaking out for the first time publicly. Voigt describes himself as an idealist, who had grand ideas to grow his business, which in 2015 had moderate earnings of R12 million. So he listed it as a Transnet preferred partner - and that’s where his story starts. CAD house was a 3d printing company and the Gupta’s approached him to partner. On paper, cad house became co-owned by gupta lieutenant - Santash Choubey - employed by Sahara Systems – but was managed as a subsidiary of the sahara group - indicating that beneficial ownership rested with the guptas themselves.SAP then entered the picture via the Guptas connection. Bernhard will explain how in August 2015 – SAP and CAD house signed a commission agreement which said: IF THE GUPTA COMPANY WERE THE “EFFECTIVE CAUSE” OF SAP LANDING A TRANSNET CONTRACT WORTH R100 MILLION OR MORE, IT WOULD GET A 10% COMMISSION FEE. NOW SALES COMMISSION AGREEMENTS AREN’T UNUSUAL AT 1 OR 2% BUT AT 10%, TO SOME, IT MAY SOUND SUSPICIOUSLY LIKE A EUPHEMISM FOR KICKBACK. AmaBhugane Journalist Susan Comrie believes so. And as a Gupta Leaks troller, she broke this story in mid 2017. In her audio recorded interview with them they claimed CAD House was no different than any other sales agent SAP uses. AmaB recorded their interview with SAPs Chief Financial Officer Deena Pillay who explained why CAD house was chosen to be SAPs strategic business partner.“They’re small guys who would go out there, identify business and come to SAP with that opportunity. It’s a lever available to SAP to sell its software… We’ve got a sales force that we employ, so these are the agents on the ground…"They are an extension of the sales force.” But if you speak to Bernard he says they never had experience marketing or selling SAP software- they're just a 3d printing company.

Summary:
In SAPs world, commission agreements are not unusual. Except in this case Transnet was already a client of SAP and the commission agreement with CAD House made it clear SAP was not so much as a sales agent to market a product to Transnet as a fixer to clinch the deal. IN EARLY 2016 SAP’S INTERNAL MEMOS ACKNOWLEDGED THAT ITS GLOBAL PRACTICE OF PAYING “BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT PARTNERS” TO SECURE DEALS - WAS FRAUGHT WITH RISK OF CORRUPTION. CAD House’s “main purpose”, it specified, “is to assist [SAP] in obtaining Customer consent to the Customer Contract and Customer’s requisite signatures to such agreement”. In the audio interview with SAP they say: “We were doing a proof of concept and CAD house was an existing vendor at Transnet and we were looking at doing 3D models for these guys to show them the value and the benefit of using our solution… The deal…" But what makes SAPs claims more awkward is the fact that Transnet deny it had any relationship with CAD house whatsoever. AND CADhouse says they never made 3d models of traing, and if they had, at most it would have been R50,000 job. Not 100 million rand. He will also tell us how despite SAP claiming due diligence was done, it wasn't. They never even met him. SAPs initial due diligence report never mentioned the Guptas - which is strange considering a simple consumer search would have shown their ownership - and a google search would have been peppered with words like “corruption.” However, no red flags were raised. The first Transnet contract SAP was awarded was R114 million… of which R17 million was paid into CAD house’s account… that money was then moved into a Gupta entity.

Further information:
Susan will show us the easy money trail they made and we have some amazing link opportunities. Bernard will confirm that CAD house used as a front for the guptas to funnel money out of SAP to gain a contract with Transnet - as well as telling us his personal story, how this affected him, how this made his life so difficult afterwards. ON THE DAY CAD HOUSE RECEIVED THE MONEY, THE VERY FIRST THING THEY DID IS PAY R2 MILLION PLUS VAT TO BIRSAA PROJECT, A FRONT COMPANY CONTROLLED BY THE GUPTA EMPIRE, WHOSE ADDRESS WAS A MAILBOX. After the Gupta Leaks revelations, SAP defended its decision to hire CAD house, saying they added real sales value, and weren’t simply a channel to exert undue influence to secure contracts. But that position became harder to believe when due diligence reports commissioned by SAP at the same time screamed red flag words like Zuma, Gupta’s, state capture…SAP put the contracts on hold. However Bernard will explain that if you look at the contract – it said that SAP could at any time come and audit their financials, and had they, they would have seen the money flowed into the account the one day, and into a Gupta linked company the next. They didn’t want to know!!! YOU’D THINK THE STORY WOULD END THERE, BUT WITH A SUCCESSFUL TRANSNET DEAL IN THE BAG, SAP’S SALES TEAM ALERTED THEM TO AN IRRESISTIBLE OPPORTUNITY: A SOFTWARE DEAL WORTH HUNDREDS OF MILLIONS - THIS TIME WITH ESKOM. But that opportunity was in danger of being scuppered, so damage control led SAP to launch an investigation, and order CAD House to cut ties with the Guptas. The Guptas stake was sold to IT company Futureteq… but had SAP looked closer they’d have seen it was formed 4 days prior to the sale, and was owned by another SAHARA employee… Around the same time, SAPs global compliance internal memos warned staff of shell companies: making sure contractors were “properly funded and resourced IT companies, and not just a shell company that was newly formed weeks or even days before a deal…” BUT IT SEEMED WORTH THE RISK, IT PAID OFF: AT THE HEIGHT OF STATE CAPTURE, SAP WALKED INTO THE MOST CAPTURED SOE - ESKOM - AND WALKED OUT WITH ONE OF THEIR BIGGEST DEALS IN THEIR 28 YEAR HISTORY... HALF A BILLION RANDS’ WORTH SOFTWARE SOLUTIONS. But the Gupta share would not be 10%, but effectively 25%... and on the eve of the deal, SAPs own lawyers coincidentally warned them of this long list of laws they would be breaking - including a billion rand fine or a life sentence in jail. One last warning that should have been heard all the way in SAPs German headquarters should have been then-public protector Thuli Madonsela’s State of Capture report, which painted an astonishing picture of SOEs being milked. But a week later SAP global Robert Enslin, president of SAPS cloud business and a member of SAPs global board put pen to paper and signed the deal. SAP PAID THE R78 MILLION COMMISSION FEE TO CADHOUSE, WHICH WAS THEN DISBURSED TO THE GUPTAS COMPANIES, THEIR TWO INDIAN BANKS AND THE OBSCURE LETTERBOX COMPANY… CAD HOUSE GOT NOTHING. Berhard will explain how his company was hijacked and used. He will also tell us about the parties and how in the meantime the Gupta’s were living the high life…
But the R100 million laundered through CAD house did not only relate to Transnet AND Eskom, SAP said they paid CAD house in respect of other customers too. SAP had deals with transnet, eskom… city of joburg… department of water and sanitation in 2017 an EFF whistleblower published allegations that SAP paid R35 million in kickbacks to secure a contract with SAP. THIS TELLS US that SAP signed up for exactly the same service other transnational companies had – (companies like neotel, Liebherr, China South Rail, McKinsey, T-systems – the leaks have shown 7 companies) making this a standard business practice, not an exception, but the rule.
Four SAP local executive heads rolled since the revelations, and SAP promised continuous transparency with their findings...BUT IN A SHOCKING REVELATION BERNHARD REVEALS THAT SAP HAVE NEVER EVEN COME TO INTERVIEW HIM FOR THE THEIR INTENSIVE AND TRANSPARENT INVESTIGATION!!!!

AS SAP IS LISTED IN AMERICA, IT FALLS UNDER US JURISDICTION AND IS SUBJECT TO THEIR ANTI-BRIBERY AND ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING LAWS. IT WILL BE UP TO THE US DEPARTMENT OF JUSTICE TO DEICE WHETHER SAP EXECUTIVES “DELIBERATELY CLOSED THEIR EYES” TO CORRUPTION. With the Gupta’s fleeing the country and going to Dubai, their media and computer complex ONLY HAVE “media house” for sale signs... However the SUI says they are working with the NPA to bring the brothers back to South Africa to stand trial. Transnet said they did not make any payments to third parties and has no knowledge of the alleged transactions. Part of the company investigation entailed approaching suppliers for their perspective on the allegations, and should any actionable facts arise, remedial action will be taken. THE SIU CONFIRMED THEY ARE INVESTIGATING SOFTWARE CONTRACTS AT ESKOM...BUT ALSO AT THE DEPARTMENT OF WATER AND THERE ARE INVESTIGATION AT THE CITY OF JOBURG SAP TENDER ETC...they didn't use the gupta's for those contracts... so it's likely it wasn't a GUPTA problem but an SAP one.

Might need Thomas for one day - he's R7,250 - but it would be worth it in this case as story requires beautiful visuals.

Script:


This small business located in Johannesburg prints in 3D and sells a variety of 3d printers. It grew from owner Bernhard Vogts garage into a profitable company with moderate earnings of R12 million.
Vogt: I started CAD house about 10 years ago, out of necessity, I went through retrenchment. And it very quickly grew into something quite big in the 3D printing business in South Africa.
In 2015 CAD house was preapproved to be on the Transnet and Eskom vendor supply list which is where Vogts cautionary tale begins. This is the first time he’s speaking publicly about the events that followed.
Bernhard: That's when SAHARA systems approached us.
All Vogt says he knew about Sahara’s owner the Gupta brothers at that time was the landing of their plane at Waterkloof airforce base for the controversial wedding.
Masa: At that point did you know the link with the guptas?
B: No we didn't really, we knew about the Guptas, they seem like such nice guys. Tony Gupta, I was in his office. He welcomed me in and hugged me and yeah. Yeah he wants to to help me grow into this into a big business and it all looks so good. Almost too good.
This was before the 2016 Public Protector Thuli Madonsela’s investigation into State Capture. Which showed at Transnet: Ajay, Atul and Rajesh Gupta had gained access to a billion rand deal. And at Eskom, the brothers' close proximity to then-President Jacob Zuma helped them control eskom's board to extract tenders worth billions. Two years, a Commission of Inquiry began to unpack all the allegations into State Capture...
Judge Zondo: “If it is successful it does have the potential of making a serious contribution in various matters that are of great concern.”
IT’S UNKNOWN HOW MANY BILLIONS STATE CAPTURE HAS COST SOUTH AFRICA’S ECONOMY. BUT THIS STORY IS NOT JUST A GUPTA ONE, IT’S ABOUT INTERNATIONAL COMPANIES SEEMINGLY USING THE GUPTA SERVICE TO PROFIT, AND THEN STAYING “WILFULLY BLIND” AFTER THE FACT.
SAP video, Clive Owen: “I’ve been thinking about thinking...
Enter German Software company SAP - who sell software solutions in 180 countries.
Clive Owen: “What if a business could turn all that thinking into doing? I can think of one. (SAP sign)
Listed on the New York stock exchange, the multinational earned R450 billion last year.
YOU’D THINK A GIANT MULTINATIONAL SOFTWARE COMPANY LIKE SAP COULD CLOSE BIG DEALS WITH OUR SOE’S ON ITS OWN,
But documents show they collaborated with the brothers using their political influence. On paper, CAD House became co-owned by gupta lieutenant - Santash Choubey - employed by Sahara Systems – but was managed as a subsidiary of the Sahara Group - indicating that beneficial ownership rested with the guptas themselves.
Bernhard: They operated all of the financials and books and all that. I did retain my signing powers. But and there was a contract I had to sign which said I wouldn't. And there was a contract that I had to change the banking logging rights so that I could only view accounts.
Masa: Where does then SAP and the venture come into the equation here?
Bernhard: We got approached and they said ‘listen we need a development partner.’ I was brought a contract to sign which basically gave us a commission share and I signed it, and that was that.
This contract bizarrely turned the simple 3d printing company into a sales agent for the software giant.
IF THE GUPTA COMPANY WERE THE “EFFECTIVE CAUSE” OF SAP LANDING A TRANSNET CONTRACT WORTH R100 MILLION OR MORE, IT WOULD GET A 10% COMMISSION FEE.” A SALES OF COMMISSION OF 1 OR 2% MAY BE UNDERSTANDABLE, BUT THIS WAS 10%... AND TO SOME, IT MAY SOUND SUSPICIOUSLY LIKE A EUPHEMISM FOR KICKBACK.
Investigative Journalist Susan Comrie believes so. AmaBhungane...the not for profit investigative unit that put state capture on the map... broke this story in mid 2017.
Susan: “The basic headline that everyone knows is that is SAP one of the world's largest software companies got caught paying what appeared to be kickbacks to Gupta controlled companies in order to secure business from some of the big state owned companies.”
In Amabhungane’s transcript from their interview with SAPs Africa Chief Financial Officer Deena Pillay, he reiterates that the contract with CAD House strangely makes them an official software sales agent.
Deena Pillay: “They’re small guys who would go out there, identify business and come to SAP with that opportunity. It’s a lever available to SAP to sell its software… They are an extension of the sales force.”
The contract adds that the 3d printing business was somehow to influence our government into giving SAP tenders.
Masa: Were you a strategic business partner?
Bernhard: No.
Masa: What influence would you have had?
Bernhard: We had no expertise. Nothing at all.
Being a legitimate transnet vendor placed cadhouse in the perfect position to be used by the Guptas to gain access to the parastatal’s coffers.
Masa: Now CAD House would have to present this to the CFO of transnet, did you deliver any of this?
Bernhard: That’s not something I have any knowledge about, its not something I could propose to anyone.
SAP then paid 17 million rand to CAD house - their commission fee of the R114 million Transnet contract.
Bernhard: When the first payments came in and I saw the size of these payments. That was more than our entire turnover for the full year in one transaction. I was like ‘something's wrong, we didn't do anything for this?’
Susan: If CAD House had done the work you would expect CAD House to be the beneficiary of that. Instead payments start flowing out and you have large round amounts going out that starts looking like CAD House is being used as a cog in a kind of money laundering scheme.
ON THE DAY CAD HOUSE RECEIVED THE MONEY, THE VERY FIRST THING THEY DID IS PAY R2 MILLION PLUS VAT TO A FRONT COMPANY CONTROLLED BY A GHOST IT SEEMS, WHOSE BUSINESS ADDRESS LEADS US TO THESE RANDOM LETTER BOXES.
Susan: effectively it's a company that exists on paper, but it doesn't really have any physical presence. If SAP had done further digging, where the money was going from CAD House, which they were entitled to do in terms of their contract that's when they would have seen these letterbox companies starting to appear.
SAPs Pillay explained to Amabhungane that the commission paid to CAD House was absurdly for 3D models of trains.
Pillay: “We were doing a proof of concept and CAD house was an existing vendor at Transnet and we were looking at doing 3D models for these guys to show them the value and the benefit of using our solution…
Masa: Did you at any point design 3D model trains?
Bernhard: (Laughs) Not that I'm aware of, no.
Masa: Is there any work that you're doing that is actually granted for any of this money?
Bernhard: Not at all. I was told if there's any inquiry from SAP to direct it to one of the other directors. I was basically told by my auditors listen, as long as you didn't benefit from this yourself, you've reported it, and you fine.
SAPs Pillay’s claim seems more questionable when Transnet stated it had no relationship with CAD House whatsoever. At the same time an SAP due diligence report told them exactly who they were doing business with.
Susan: The due diligence is kind of peppered with words about state capture about how the guptas use their connections with the president and with President Son to to effectively get these contracts out of state owned companies. So they basically say you know we're not going to carry on doing any business for now with these companies.
So Choubey’s shares in CAD House were conveniently sold to another IT company...predictably it had been registered 4 days prior, and was owned by another SAHARA employee…
Bernhard: We all knew, it was just a change of name and a change of different directors.
LINK 6: YOU’D THINK THE STORY WOULD END THERE, BUT SAP’S SALES TEAM ALERTED THEM TO AN IRRESISTIBLE OPPORTUNITY: A SOFTWARE DEAL WORTH HUNDREDS OF MILLIONS - THIS TIME WITH ESKOM.
Susan: it's kind of the all you can eat buffet equivalent of software. before the contract is signed. the Public Protector Report comes out. Did anyone at SAP see that report? Seemingly they don't because what happens is over the next week or so a kind of a whole list of people within SAP sign off on that deal.
Including Global SAP board member Robert Enslin. And this time, the commission increased to 25% of a half billion rands worth of software - roughly 74 million. This means that in total SAP walked away with R600 million rands worth of tenders, and the Guptas were paid R100 million rand in alleged kickbacks.
Susan: There's an email from the local compliance officer in South Africa writing to the head of global compliance, and it's not even 6:00 a.m. in the morning, sending up a flag and saying look there's a chance the Gupta’s are still in the background. Do we want to go ahead with this deal? And the response from global compliance is effectively two lines sent from her iPhone to say. Great work. I approve let's go ahead.
AT THE HEIGHT OF STATE CAPTURE, SAP WALKED INTO THE MOST CAPTURED SOE - ESKOM - AND WALKED OUT WITH ONE OF THEIR BIGGEST DEALS IN THEIR ALMOST 40 YEAR HISTORY IN SA.
Susan: With Transnet with Eskom these are well-established SAP clients. These are clients that they've had for years. Why did they need the Guptas?
Masa: What are you thinking every night when you go to bed?
Bernhard: I just wanted to put it behind me... (CRY)I wasn't really interested in reporting it all going to lay claim or whatever. I was just ‘move on, move out, start again’ and that's what we did.
Did you make any money out of this?
Bernhard: No, they came to me and said ‘Listen we're gonna put R100,000 into your personal account. I knew it was tainted money, and so I refused it and I left.
Masa: Do you think you were used Bernhard?
Bernhard: Oh yeah definitely. I was used. I mean there were times where they refused to pay my staff.
Masa: Do you think you were naive as well?
Bernhard: aive and maybe a little bit desperate
In the meantime the Guptas were living the high life, and fled to their luxury palace in Dubai. The brothers and Choubey did not respond to our questions or multiple interview requests. Transnet says that they have no knowledge of the alleged transactions, and remedial action will be taken. Eskom is cooperating with law enforcement agencies like the Special Investigating Unit or SIU - and say the SAP contract will still be discussed at the Zondo Commission. Deena Pillay declined to participate in this program, saying Amabhungane interview was taken out of context, however, he and three other SAP local executives resigned. SAP launched an internal investigation.
Masa: when SAP launched the investigation did they at any point come and speak to you?
Bernhard: No, never.
WE REACHED OUT TO SAP GLOBAL, AND INITIALLY GOT A RESPONSE FROM THEIR AFRICA DIVISION, SAYING THE INVESTIGATION IS STILL ON-GOING SO THEY CANNOT COMMENT ON THE MATTER.
We then received a response from Global to say they will provide an update at an appropriate time, and asked for us to be patient.
Susan: It looks like it's not only when SAP was dealing with the Gupta's that they had these problematic contracts. If you look at what they're being investigated for with you the Department of Water Affairs contract where they're accused of effectively paying a kickback to a front company. It's not just a Gupta story. This is something far more fundamental about how they do business not just in South Africa but how they do business all over the world
